description: The arithmetic of a ContextUsageSnapshot: what a section contributes, what the whole context measures, how the rounded shares stay honest, whether the budget is exceeded and which sections a compaction can actually drop. Nothing here touches markup, so the five decisions that are easy to get wrong are testable on their own — and a host computing the same numbers elsewhere cannot drift from the component. Shares uses the largest-remainder method, so the rounded percentages add up to exactly 100 (or keep the plain floors when the entries do not account for the whole total).
usageExample:
var used = ContextUsageMath.UsedTokens(snapshot);          // 14 000
var percent = ContextUsageMath.BudgetPercent(snapshot);    // 88, null when the budget is unknown
var over = ContextUsageMath.IsOverBudget(snapshot);        // false at exactly 100 %
var shares = ContextUsageMath.Shares([1_200, 800, 6_000], used);  // 9, 6, 43 … sums to 100
var compactable = ContextUsageMath.IsCompactable(snapshot);
